issues.description: The problem statement first instructs that SealSaloon has a final Stock stock initialized in the constructor (instance field) but later explicitly states that the stock attribute must be static (shared across all instances). This is a direct contradiction about the attribute's nature and where/how it should be initialized, which will confuse students when implementing initialization and getters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: either (A) require a static final Stock (shared) and state it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer and that related methods/getters can be static, or (B) require an instance final Stock initialized in the constructor and remove the note that stock must be static. Update all references (including example code) to reflect the chosen design.

issues.description: The problem text requires a modifiable List<Meal> attribute called orders initialized in the constructor, but the provided solution (and the template code style) uses a Meal[] array for orders and array-based helpers. This mismatch between the requested type (List) and the array-based template/solution can confuse students about which collection type to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify which collection type students should use. Either change the problem statement to allow/encourage an array-based orders implementation (and reference ArrayHelpers) or update the template to include and use List<Meal> (e.g., import java.util.ArrayList and initialize orders = new ArrayList<>()) and adjust helper usage accordingly.
